messages:
sam-infra: Heads up — since ~03:20 UTC we're seeing intermittent failures from model-serving pods in us-west-2 when they hit our S3-backed model cache via interface endpoint. Some requests succeed, others time out and fall back to NAT, causing cross-AZ egress and billing spikes.

lina-sre: Repro steps? logs? error codes?

sam-infra: Quick paste from affected pod: 
```
2026-03-18T03:22:14Z ERROR http: GET https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/model.bin -> dial tcp 10.10.5.23:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-18T03:22:14Z WARN fallback: using nat-gw egress -> 52.23.xx.xx
```
No 5xx from backend, just TCP timeouts. Happens across two AZs but only for this interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.s3).

raj-eng: Did we recently change the endpoint's security group or NACLs?

sam-infra: I checked — SG attached to the ENIs only has 443 egress allowed to 0.0.0.0/0 and the service's prefix list. NACLs unchanged. Route tables: the subnet route table has the interface endpoint's prefix route pointing to local, nothing funky.

katie-netops: @sam-infra can you paste `ip route` and `curl -v` output from a repro pod? Want to see if traffic is hitting ENI or being SNAT'd.

sam-infra: pasted below — curl times out when resolv returns the private hosted zone answer. When I force public endpoint it works.
```
# ip route
default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0
10.0.0.0/16 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.5.42
169.254.169.254 via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0

# curl -v https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/model.bin
* Rebuilt URL to: https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/model.bin/
* Trying 10.12.23.45...
* connect to 10.12.23.45 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
```

lina-sre: 10.12.23.45 looks like an ENI IP in another AZ. Could be that ENI got recycled and SG lost association? Or route propagation stale in CNI plugin?

jen-support: Noted billing alert for egress spike at 03:25 UTC — +0.4TB cross-AZ. Filed ticket to finance to hold off chargeback until we root cause.

katie-netops: Check interface endpoint health in VPC Console: if the endpoint's ENIs exist but aren't healthy on the AZ, AWS will still return private IPs in split-horizon DNS but they might drop packets. Also check endpoint's security groups: were there multiple SGs created by automation recently?

sam-infra: I see two ENIs for the endpoint: ena-0a1 and ena-0b2. ena-0a1 is fine, ena-0b2 shows lots of drop counts on our flow logs. SG for endpoint is a shared sg-ep-s3 which was recently updated by infra-automation to add 443 allow from a prefix list. Before update it allowed ephemeral 1024-65535 too. Could that explain asymmetric return traffic?

raj-eng: If endpoint SG disallows ephemeral source ports on the ENI, the TCP handshake could succeed but subsequent ephemeral responses from AWS side may get blocked. But SGs evaluate statefully, so outbound reply should be allowed if initial was accepted... hmm.

lina-sre: Another possibility: our IPtables conntrack on the host hitting capacity so some flows get dropped to ENI and then timeout. Have we seen conntrack spikes?

sam-infra: Looking at node metrics: conntrack_used spiked to 220k around 03:20, limit is 256k. Not full, but two pods on that node reported "conntrack: table full" in dmesg earlier.

katie-netops: That's useful. Could be a coincident of heavy model downloads + ephemeral port restriction causing new connections to be dropped. Two-hit failure vector. Let's check flow logs for denied actions.

sam-infra: Flow log snippet (VPC flow logs):
```
2026-03-18T03:21:58Z eni-ena-0b2 10.12.23.45:443 10.0.5.42:52344 REJECT OK tcp
2026-03-18T03:22:00Z eni-ena-0b2 10.12.23.45:443 10.0.5.43:52347 REJECT OK tcp
```
REJECT indicates SG/NACL blocking on the ENI.

raj-eng: If the ENI SG rejects inbound responses, service can't talk to our pod. Why would SG reject? The ENI SG should allow ephemeral source ports back. Maybe automation switched SG to only allow from prefix list on 443 and removed the rule allowing our VPC CIDR?

katie-netops: Confirmed — infra-automation PR two days ago changed sg-ep-s3 to remove the VPC-wide inbound rule and added a narrower prefix-list entry. That would mean the ENI no longer allows inbound from our pod IP range. Because interface endpoints require you to allow traffic from your VPC to the endpoint SG.

sam-infra: Ok that explains it. How did autoscaling not catch this? Some endpoints in other subnets still had old SG attached (retrogression) so they worked, hence intermittent behavior.

lina-sre: Fix plan: 1) revert automated SG change to include inbound from VPC CIDR for HTTPS ephemeral range; 2) roll a tenant-level check to validate endpoint SGs; 3) add a runtime alert when flow logs show REJECT on eni for service-prefix.

katie-netops: I'll roll the revert now. Patching sg-ep-s3 to add inbound tcp 1024-65535 from 10.0.0.0/16 and 443 from prefix-list.

deploy-bot: @katie-netops performed change sg-ep-s3 +rules (ID:chg-2026-0318-1) — audit link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/ec2/v2/home?region=us-west-2#SecurityGroup:sg-ep-s3

sam-infra: Testing after revert — immediate improvement. curl succeeds and requests hit ENI IPs. No more NAT fallback.

jen-support: Billing alert cleared. Egress returned to baseline.

raj-eng: Follow-ups: add an automated guard in infra-automation to not remove VPC inbound for service endpoints, and add an infra test that resolves the endpoint DNS and attempts TLS handshake from a probe pod in each AZ.

lina-sre: Also add conntrack monitoring per-node + proactive scale when conntrack_used > 70%.

sam-infra: Will open infra-automation PR and a postmortem doc. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:

katie-netops: FYI — AWS recommended pattern in docs: endpoint SG must allow the VPC CIDR ephemeral ports. doc: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/endpoint-services-overview.html

sam-infra: Adding to incident ticket. Marking resolved for now.

jen-support: closing billing hold, tagging finance.

lina-sre: Good postmortem action items. I'll draft an incident summary tomorrow.
